item.title: RBI: Three payment Directions: card-based transactions, cash withdrawal at ATMs and PoS, and White Label ATM operators
item.description:
RBI · Directions

Who it covers: As stated in each Direction (card issuers and acquirers, banks, ATM and PoS operators, White Label ATM operators).

  • RBI issued three Directions on 27-11-2026: Digital Payments (Card-based transaction) Directions, Cash Withdrawal Transactions through ATMs and PoS Directions, and White Label ATM Operators Directions, all 2026.
  • The Directions are listed on RBI's Master Directions page; read each text for the operative requirements and commencement.

item.title: RBI: UAPA section 51A: two updates to the UN Security Council sanctions lists
item.description:
RBI · Notification · RBI/2026-27/308 and RBI/2026-27/309

Effective 2026-11-26.

Who it covers: Banks, NBFCs, asset reconstruction companies and All India Financial Institutions.

  • The UNSC committee amended 81 entries on its ISIL (Da'esh) and Al-Qaida sanctions list (press release of 20-11-2026); a second notification amends one further entry.
  • Regulated entities must update their screening lists and act under Chapter IX of the KYC Directions, 2025.

Official source

item.title: RBI: Reserve Bank of India (Non-Banking Financial Companies – Securitisation Transactions) Amendment Directions, 2026
item.description:
RBI · Amendment Directions · RBI/2026-27/306; DOR.STR.REC.258/21-04-177/2026-27

Effective 2027-04-01.

Who it covers: NBFCs covered by para 3 of the NBFC Securitisation Transactions Directions 2025: NBFC-D, NBFC-ICC, NBFC-Factor, NBFC-MFI, NBFC-IFC, IDF-NBFC and HFCs (para 3(vii)), all layers. Outside para 3: CICs, MGCs, NBFC-P2P, NBFC-AA, NOFHCs, SPDs and Type I NBFCs, so an Upper Layer CIC is not covered as originator. Direct assignments of loans fall under the separate Transfer of Loan Exposures Directions and are not affected. The same changes were made on the same day for commercial banks, SFBs and AIFIs (RBI/2026-27/304, 305, 307).

  • para 26 (substituted): the issuance, holding and subsequent transfer of securitisation notes must be in dematerialised form only. The ₹1 crore minimum ticket size applies at issue and at every later transfer. The originator must ensure that its agreement with the SPE requires the SPE to put in place arrangements with entities such as the registrar, depository and stock exchange, "as may be applicable", to secure the minimum ticket size. Proviso: notes with amortisation structures may be traded at amortised value if the ticket size falls below ₹1 crore. Explanation: ticket size is the investment of a single investor.
  • para 27 (substituted): for an offer of securitisation notes to the public, Regulation 21 of the SEBI (Issue and Listing of Securitised Debt Instruments and Security Receipts) Regulations 2008 must be complied with. RBI's own earlier wording (listing "recommended, though not mandatory"; offers to fifty or more persons to be listed) is removed, so the SEBI Regulations now decide what is a public offer.
  • para 27A (new): transactions in notes issued before 01-04-2027 must also comply with paras 26 and 27. There is no grandfathering for older notes.
  • Effective 01-04-2027 (para 3). Press release 2026-2027/1550 says this finalises the draft of 27-07-2026 after comments.

Official source

item.title: RBI: Governor meets MDs and CEOs of select NBFCs, HFCs and industry bodies
item.description:
RBI · Meeting (press release) · Press Release 2026-2027/1554

Who it covers: Select NBFCs (including Government NBFCs), HFCs and MFIs. Sa-Dhan, MFIN and FIDC took part, and the NHB MD & CEO attended. No new directions were issued.

  • The Governor stressed responsible and sustainable credit growth, fair recovery practices, use of CKYCR for onboarding, and a comprehensive, risk-based approach to cyber and IT risk.

Official source

item.title: RBI: Draft Amendment Directions on 'Preventive Safeguards for Electronic Banking Transactions (EBTs)'
item.description:
RBI · Draft Amendment Directions (for comment) · Press Release 2026-2027/1548

Who it covers: Seven drafts amending the Responsible Business Conduct Directions for commercial banks, SFBs, payments banks, LABs, RRBs, UCBs and RCBs. No NBFC or HFC draft. Comments due by 14-12-2026.

  • Seven draft amendments to the banks' Responsible Business Conduct Directions. Per the press release, they aim to give customers greater control over how and how far their digital payment channels can be used, and to widen the definition of "negligence by a bank" in the 24-06-2026 customer-liability amendment.
  • The press release does not describe the detailed proposals; they are in the seven draft documents.

Official source

item.title: RBI: RBI imposes monetary penalty on an NBFC
item.description:
RBI · Enforcement (press release) · Press Release 2026-2027/1537 (order dated 17-11-2026)

Who it covers: Another lender (described as an NBFC in secondary sources). It is a routine enforcement order and creates no new rule.

  • Penalty of ₹7.50 lakh by order of 17-11-2026, under RBI Act s.58G(1)(b) read with s.58B(5)(aa), following a statutory inspection of the position as on 31-03-2026.
  • Findings: the company failed to obtain PAN (or its e-document) or Form 60 when establishing account-based relationships, and failed to escalate partly or wholly rejected complaints to the Internal Ombudsman within the prescribed time. RBI cites its KYC and Internal Ombudsman directions without paragraph numbers.

Official source

item.title: RBI: 13 NBFCs and one HFC surrender their registrations
item.description:
RBI · Enforcement (press release) · Press Release 2026-2027/1500

Who it covers: The entities named in the press release.

  • RBI cancelled the registrations on surrender: six entities exited the non-banking financial business, five met the criteria for unregistered Type I status, and three ceased to exist as legal entities.
  • The HFC registration was cancelled under section 29A of the National Housing Bank Act.

Official source

item.title: RBI: Certificates of Registration of 49 NBFCs cancelled
item.description:
RBI · Enforcement (press release) · Press Release 2026-2027/1501

Who it covers: The NBFCs named in the press release; lenders and partners dealing with them.

  • RBI cancelled the registration of 49 NBFCs under section 45-IA(6) of the RBI Act, by orders passed in October 2026.
  • A separate release of 09-11-2026 announced one more cancellation.
  • An entity whose registration is cancelled cannot carry on the business of a non-banking financial institution.

Official source

item.title: RBI: Monetary penalty on a prepaid payment instrument issuer
item.description:
RBI · Enforcement (press release) · Press Release 2026-2027/1496

Who it covers: A non-bank prepaid payment instrument issuer.

  • Penalty of ₹9.00 lakh under section 30 of the Payment and Settlement Systems Act, by order dated 06-11-2026.
  • Findings: fund transfers by wallet holders to beneficiaries that were not pre-registered went beyond the permitted limit, and frauds were not reported to RBI in time.

Official source

item.title: RBI: Domestic Money Transfer Directions, 2026
item.description:
RBI · Directions · RBI/DPSS/2026-27/476

Effective 2026-11-11.

Who it covers: Banks, authorised payment system operators and participants offering domestic money transfer. Card-to-card transfers are excluded.

  • Cash pay-out is capped at ₹10,000 per transaction and ₹25,000 a month per beneficiary; walk-in customers may remit up to ₹50,000 by NEFT.
  • Cash-based remittance through business correspondents and ATMs is capped at ₹5,000 per transaction and ₹25,000 a month per remitter.
  • The remitter is registered using a verified mobile number and a self-certified officially valid document, and every transaction needs an additional factor of authentication.
  • The IMPS or NEFT message must carry the remitter's details and an identifier marking it as a cash-based remittance.
  • The circulars of 05-10-2011 and 24-07-2024 are repealed.

Official source

item.title: RBI: Draft consolidated Priority Sector Lending Directions for banks
item.description:
RBI · Draft Directions (for comment) · Press Release 2026-2027/1447

item.title: RBI: Master Directions on Cyber Resilience and Digital Payment Security Controls for non-bank Payment System Operators
item.description:
RBI · Directions · RBI/DPSS/2026-27/475

Effective 2026-11-05.

Who it covers: Non-bank payment system operators: in force on issue for large and medium operators, and from 01-04-2028 for small operators.

  • Consolidates the 2024 Master Directions with the earlier circulars on ATM switch application service providers and system-audit scope.
  • A Board sub-committee reviews cyber risk every quarter; the information-security policy is reviewed every year.
  • Unusual incidents such as cyber-attacks and outages of critical systems are reported to RBI within six hours of detection; audit logs are kept for five years.
  • The annual System Audit Report is filed within two months of the financial year end.
  • Operators must make sure the unregulated entities in their payment chain follow the controls.
  • The Master Direction on Payment Aggregators was updated on 11-11-2026 to refer to these Directions.

Official source
